sections.heading: What is register?
sections.body: Register is the level of formality in language. In English, the same idea can be expressed in different ways depending on the situation and the person you are talking to. Choosing the right register is essential at B2 level.

sections.heading: Idioms for informal register
list: It's a piece of cake. (= very easy)
Once in a blue moon. (= very rarely)
Cost an arm and a leg. (= very expensive)

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not use contractions in formal writing: 'I'm' → 'I am'.
Do not use slang or idioms in formal essays.
Do not mix registers in the same text.

phases.name: Discovery
phases.intro: Look at these sentences. Read them carefully and think about the questions below.
sentences: I would like to enquire about your courses.
I apologise for the delay in replying.
Thanks a lot for your help!
The exam was a piece of cake.
I would be grateful if you could send me more information.

questions: Which sentences are formal and which are informal?
In sentence 1, how does 'enquire' compare with 'ask'?
In sentence 4, how would you rewrite it formally?
In sentence 6, what does 'a piece of cake' mean literally and idiomatically?
In sentence 7, why is 'I would be grateful if' more polite than 'Can you'?
What is the main difference between formal and informal register?

sections.heading: Key rules
list: Three registers: informal (friends), neutral (everyday), formal (work, academic).
Formal vocabulary: obtain, purchase, require, assist, enquire, inform, apologise.
Formal structures: I would be grateful if..., I look forward to..., Please find attached...
Do not mix registers in the same text.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not use contractions in formal writing.
Do not use idioms in essays or business emails.
Keep the register consistent throughout the text.
